title: Support criterion for restriction of a right adjoint to a quasi-compact open
statement: Let f:X\to Y be a morphism of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let a be the right adjoint to Rf_* on quasi-coherent derived categories [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-direct-image], and let V\subset Y be a quasi-compact open with inverse image U=f^{-1}(V)\subset X, with open immersions j:V\to Y and j_U:U\to X. Let a_V be the right adjoint for the restriction f|_U:U\to V. The canonical open-square map j_U^*a(K)\to a_V(Lj^*K) is an isomorphism for every K\in D_QCoh^+(Y) if and only if a(Q) is supported on X\setminus U for every Q\in D_QCoh^+(Y) supported on Y\setminus V. The same equivalence holds with D_QCoh(Y) in place of D_QCoh^+(Y). If a commutes with all set-indexed direct sums, the bounded-below equivalent conditions imply (and hence are equivalent to) the unbounded equivalent conditions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-right-adjoint-open-unit-cone-test] separately to each K. It supplies a supported Q, bounded below whenever K is, and identifies invertibility of the specified restricted a-unit with vanishing of the restricted a-image of Q. The unit and all binder types stay the ones written in the original Lean statement.

For a supported object K, its open restriction is zero, so Rj_*j^*K is zero. Additivity of derived direct image and adjoint additivity imply that a takes this zero object to zero. The lifted object is zero because the full-subcategory inclusion is faithful. Hence the restricted a-unit at K is invertible if and only if its source is zero. Use this converse together with the pointwise cone test to prove both universal equivalences, using the cone lower bound in the bounded-below case.

When a preserves all set-indexed sums, apply [lem-sc-right-adjoint-open-support-of-bounded] to the bounded support condition obtained by the first equivalence. Apply the unbounded equivalence to obtain the unbounded isomorphism condition. The reverse direction simply restricts the universal isomorphism condition to bounded-below objects.

proof_origin.note: Complete Lean proof of all three clauses from the proved pointwise cone test, the proved zero-object converse, and the proved perfect-generator support extension. No new sorry is left.
